reasons: The target appeal cannot be allowed because the lease deed is unregistered and inadmissible under the Registration Act, 1908, preventing the tenant from relying on any clause granting consent for sub-letting or assignment. (Source: 69305:p0005.s002; Condition: Unregistered lease deed.)

The tenant's argument that the amalgamation was compelled by FERA is unproven, as the Reserve Bank issued a direction only to reduce share capital, not to mandate amalgamation, leaving the transfer of possession voluntary and liable for eviction. (Source: p0003.s007; Condition: Specific RBI direction for amalgamation.)

The court must determine if the tenant factually parted with possession; since the tenant failed to prove the landlord's specific written consent for the sub-letting, the statutory ground for eviction under Section 14(1)(b) remains unmet. (Source: 69305:p0005.s003; Condition: Written consent for specific sub-letting.)
missing: Whether the landlord obtained specific written consent for the sub-letting/assignment in favor of the Indian Company, as general consent clauses in unregistered deeds are inadmissible. (Condition: Written consent specificity.)
Whether the tenant can prove the amalgamation was strictly compulsory under FERA rather than a voluntary corporate strategy to comply with shareholding limits. (Condition: Compulsion vs. Volition.)

Whether the tenant factually parted with possession of the premises, as the tenant's claim of 'no parting' contradicts the landlord's evidence of exclusive possession by the new entity. (Condition: Factual possession status.)
